summary: Material changes since the prior snapshot: U.S.-China agreed to extend the Busan trade agreement until January 10; U.S.-Iran diplomacy remained active but far apart and Hormuz reopening stayed conditional; Brent settled back above $103. Official U.S. Treasury September 23 yields rose sharply, with 2Y 4.85% and 10Y 5.11%. U.S. flash composite PMI reached 58.4, a more-than-five-year high, with stronger orders and price pressure. No new CPI/PCE/NFP/claims/ISM, Taiwan official activity release, or China PMI release was found.

macro_summary.taiwan_equity_implication: Taiwan export-order strength and the temporary U.S.-China trade-truce extension support external-demand visibility, but the U.S. 10Y above 5%, stronger U.S. activity/price pressure and renewed oil gains raise discount-rate and input-cost headwinds. Middle East de-escalation remains possible but unconfirmed.
macro_summary.notes: Official numeric series remain authoritative; semantic scores are research evidence only. S&P Global flash PMI is tracked as supplemental growth evidence and does not replace ISM.

key_drivers.name: U.S.-China Busan agreement extension
key_drivers.observed: Bessent said the U.S. and China agreed September 23 to extend the Busan Agreement until January 10.
key_drivers.interpretation: Near-term tariff/trade escalation risk falls, but the extension is temporary and does not settle technology, Taiwan or critical-mineral disputes.

key_drivers.name: U.S. growth and rates reprice higher
key_drivers.observed: September flash composite PMI rose to 58.4 from 56.0; official Treasury September 23 yields were 4.85% for 2Y and 5.11% for 10Y.
key_drivers.interpretation: Stronger demand is supportive for global growth but higher prices and yields are a valuation headwind for duration-sensitive Taiwan equities.

key_drivers.name: Middle East diplomacy stalls and oil rebounds
key_drivers.observed: U.S.-Iran indirect talks continued but remained far apart; Hormuz reopening stayed conditional. Brent settled at $103.08 and WTI at $92.16 on September 23.
key_drivers.interpretation: Energy-inflation and freight risks remain elevated despite active diplomacy and Saudi bypass supply recovery.

key_risks: U.S. 10Y Treasury yield rose above 5%, increasing equity discount-rate pressure.
Hormuz reopening remains conditional and U.S.-Iran positions remain far apart.
Oil rebounded sharply despite restored Saudi bypass supply.
Trump-Xi summit still carries Taiwan, technology and trade-policy tail risk despite the temporary Busan extension.
Russia-Ukraine energy infrastructure risk remains unresolved.
DXY and VIX remain stale in this semantic snapshot.

policy_tone.fed: Hawkish tightening; target 3.75%-4.00%, with stronger September activity and price pressure reinforcing restrictive-rate risk.
policy_tone.taiwan_central_bank: Hold with selective credit easing; policy rate 2.0%.
policy_tone.china: September LPR unchanged; U.S.-China Busan trade arrangement extended to January 10.
policy_tone.us_china: Near-term trade escalation risk reduced by Busan extension, while Taiwan/technology issues remain unresolved ahead of summit outcomes.
policy_tone.middle_east: Diplomacy active but no convergence or ceasefire; Hormuz reopening remains conditional and oil risk premium rebounded.
policy_tone.global: Restrictive financial conditions with strong U.S. growth signals and persistent energy/security risk.
